stories.title: Lawrence beats Stevens in MI-7 after vowing to block data centers
stories.dek: Will Lawrence defeated Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary for Michigan's 7th congressional district by campaigning against large data-center projects. The win shifts the fight over power demand, tax breaks and local land use into Congress. Voters in Washtenaw and surrounding counties now have a representative who made data-center opposition central to the race.
stories.source_title: ‘Organized People Can Beat Organized Money’: Lawrence Wins House Primary After Harnessing Opposition to Data Centers - Common Dreams

stories.title: Holland-area voters reject data-center project at the ballot box
stories.dek: Residents in a western Michigan township voted down a proposed data center, ending months of debate over noise, power use and property values. The defeat shows local opposition can stop projects even after site plans advance. Nearby communities watching similar proposals now see a clear precedent.
stories.source_title: Watch the moment voters learned they struck down a data center - The Holland Sentinel

stories.title: Mason voters narrow council field in race dominated by data-center fight
stories.dek: Eight candidates remain after Mason voters winnowed a City Council primary shaped by a proposed data center. The project has divided residents over electricity rates and industrial zoning in the Ingham County city. The November winners will decide whether the plan moves forward.
stories.source_title: Mason voters pare City Council race tied to data center to 8 candidates - Lansing State Journal

stories.title: Michigan voters elect moratorium backer, pushing data center fight into Congress
stories.dek: A candidate who campaigned against unchecked data center growth won a key Michigan House primary. The result moves local fights over power demand and tax breaks onto the national stage. Residents in districts facing new projects now have a stronger voice in Washington on grid costs and water use.
stories.source_title: Moratorium Candidate Wins House Toss-Up: Michigan Primary Shifts Data Center Fight to Congress - Tech Times

stories.title: Augusta Twp voters kill farmland rezoning for data center
stories.dek: Residents overturned a rezoning that would have allowed a data center on agricultural land. The vote keeps the property from shifting to industrial use and blocks the project from moving forward. Washtenaw County taxpayers and nearby homeowners avoid the noise, power, and water demands that would have followed.
stories.source_title: Augusta Township voters overturn Data Center rezoning - WEMU

stories.title: Independence Township passes moratorium blocking new data centers
stories.dek: Independence Township supervisors approved a moratorium that stops new data center proposals while rules are written. The pause gives the community time to decide how much power, water and land these projects can use. Oakland County residents now have a template for slowing builds in their own towns.
stories.source_title: Independence Twp. green lights moratorium on data centers - Clarkston News

stories.title: Governor faces scrutiny over billion-dollar facility lacking local approvals
stories.dek: A new report questions whether Gov. Whitmer advanced a major data center project in Saline Township before all required local permits were secured. Residents in Washtenaw County and nearby areas could see big changes in power demand, water use and tax revenue if the project moves forward. The claim puts the governor's office on the defensive just as primary voters head to the polls.
stories.source_title: Did Whitmer Push Saline Data Center Without Proper Permits? - Michigan Enjoyer

stories.title: City halts utilities deal, leaving township's data center without water supply
stories.dek: Lowell city officials suspended sewer and water negotiations with Lowell Township, halting progress on a proposed data center. Kent County residents now face uncertainty over whether the project can secure the infrastructure it needs. The move signals growing local resistance to data centers that could strain resources and raise utility rates.
stories.source_title: In blow to proposed data center, Lowell suspends water, sewer talks with Lowell Township - WOODTV.com

stories.title: Wayne County sees $6B data center proposal land on the table
stories.dek: A major new campus plan would bring thousands of construction jobs but also heavy electricity demand. Wayne County residents could see tax revenue gains alongside grid strain. Local officials have not yet scheduled a formal review.
stories.source_title: $6B data center plan unveiled in Wayne County | 28/22 News - 28/22 News

stories.title: Lowell residents lose Microsoft data center after council cites secrecy
stories.dek: The Lowell City Council stopped all talks with Microsoft over a proposed data center, saying the company failed to share enough details on power needs and local impacts. Residents in Kent County now face uncertainty over potential jobs, tax revenue, and strain on the electric grid. The decision blocks one of the few large-scale data center projects actively discussed in West Michigan this year.
stories.source_title: Microsoft data center talks halted by Lowell City Council - WZZM13.com

stories.title: Washtenaw residents file recall bids against seven officials over data centers
stories.dek: A local opponent has turned in signatures to recall seven elected officials in the Ann Arbor area. The effort stems from fights over proposed data-center projects and their effects on power, water and taxes. Voters 30 miles away will watch whether the recalls reach the ballot and shift local control.
stories.source_title: Data center opponent submits recall signatures targeting 7 elected officials near Ann Arbor - MLive.com

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
